title: Globalization

source.name: Wikipedia — Globalization
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Globalization is the process of increasing interdependence and integration among the economies, markets, societies, and cultures of different countries worldwide. It can be attributed to a series of factors, including the reduction of barriers to international trade, the liberalization of capital movements, the development of transportation infrastructure, and the advancement of information and communication technologies. The term globalization first appeared in the early 20th century, but came into popular use in the 1990s to describe the growing international connectivity of the post–Cold War world.

Large-scale globalization began in the 1820s, and in the late 19th century and early 20th century drove a rapid expansion in the connectivity of the world's economies and cultures. The origins of globalization can be traced back to the 18th and 19th centuries, a period marked by significant advancements in transportation and communication technologies following the Industrial Revolution. These developments increased global interactions, supporting the growth of international trade and the exchange of ideas, beliefs, and cultures.

Between 1990 and 2010, globalization progressed rapidly, driven by the information and communication technology revolution that lowered communication costs, along with trade liberalization and the shift of manufacturing operations to emerging economies (particularly China). Academic literature commonly divides globalization into three major areas: economic globalization, cultural globalization, and political globalization.

Proponents of globalization point to economic growth and broader societal development as benefits, while opponents claim globalizing processes are detrimental to social well-being due to ethnocentrism, environmental consequences, and other potential drawbacks.

The word globalization was used in the English language as early as the 1930s, but only ever in the context of education, and the term failed to gain traction. Over the next few decades, the term was occasionally used by other scholars and media, but it was not clearly defined. One of the first uses of a term resembling the more common meaning and usage of the modern word was by French economist François Perroux in his essays from the early 1960s (in his French works he used the similar yet distinct term mondialisation, translated as mundialization). Theodore Levitt is sometimes inaccurately cited as having invented the term in the mid-1980s, although he can more confidently be credited with popularizing the term and bringing it into the mainstream business audience during that time.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a factor behind globalization?
options: The reduction of barriers to international trade
A rapid increase in the world’s population
The advancement of information and communication technologies
questions.explain: Đoạn 1 liệt kê: giảm rào cản thương mại, tự do hóa dòng vốn, hạ tầng giao thông, công nghệ thông tin – truyền thông. Không nhắc đến dân số.

questions.q: When, according to the text, did large-scale globalization begin?
What drove the rapid progress of globalization between 1990 and 2010?
options: The information and communication technology revolution, trade liberalization and the shift of manufacturing to emerging economies
The invention of the steam engine
The creation of the United Nations
questions.explain: Đoạn 3: “driven by the information and communication technology revolution … along with trade liberalization and the shift of manufacturing operations to emerging economies”.

questions.q: How do opponents of globalization view it?
options: As harmful to social well-being because of ethnocentrism, environmental consequences and other drawbacks
As a cause of faster economic growth
As an old idea that no longer matters
As a plan made by one government
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: “opponents claim globalizing processes are detrimental to social well-being due to ethnocentrism, environmental consequences, and other potential drawbacks.”

questions.q: In paragraph 5, what does “failed to gain traction” mean?
options: Did not become widely accepted or used
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: thuật ngữ chỉ dùng trong bối cảnh giáo dục, “failed to gain traction” = không được lan rộng, không phổ biến.

questions.q: Who is more confidently credited with popularizing the term in the mid-1980s?
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: “Theodore Levitt … can more confidently be credited with popularizing the term”.

questions.q: The term globalization came into popular use in the 1990s.
questions.explain: Đoạn 1: “came into popular use in the 1990s”.

questions.q: The word globalization was first used in English in the 1990s.
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: từ này được dùng bằng tiếng Anh “as early as the 1930s”, dù chỉ trong lĩnh vực giáo dục.
